Renmin University researchers report that EditAct, which judges and revises noisy reasoning-action steps before tool execution, improved average scores by 3.2–6.7 percentage points over the strongest baseline across six benchmarks with Qwen3.5-4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B agents.
The authors released a 35-billion-parameter BF16 checkpoint and Apache-2.0 inference code; their benchmark gains are author-reported averages across three runs per benchmark.
